summary: Docs-only commit; no test files staged, so nothing to mutate. Reviewed as test PRESCRIPTIONS for M4.10c/d. Round-8 major is genuinely fixed: the ADR and the M4.10c notes now prescribe an ASSERTION on the per-segment triple rather than fixture data, and the PARTIAL hoist (podId per segment, incarnation+flushSeq per delta) is confirmed as the surviving mutation. Verified in-tree: BatchingSequencerTest:261 asserts only hasSize(2) on a two-pod commitAll whose requests both carry flushSeq 0; BatchedCommitDeltaTest's whole-record isEqualTo kills a full hoist only when a hoisted field varies; golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin holds bins/a.seg with no pod byte; Checkpoint.java:151 is `version != VERSION`; CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest:117 is bytes[7]=1 over the big-endian version int at offset 4. All three round-8 minors are in. Restore after M0.79 is clean: staged set is exactly 7 docs paths, no unstaged diff, no untracked files, and the sequencer/ingest files that were staged earlier are back at HEAD.

findings.claim: The ADR's prescribed assertion, followed literally, does not kill the partial hoist the very next sentence names. The M4.10c notes state it correctly; the ADR is one notch looser.
findings.failure_scenario: ADR-0036 says: assert 'the PER-SEGMENT triple, after round-trip and after commitAll, on a fixture whose triple varies in at least one field per segment', then names the partial hoist -- podId per segment, incarnation and flushSeq per delta -- as the mutation none of the three fixtures catches. Every fixture in the tree ALREADY satisfies 'varies in at least one field per segment', and the field it varies in is podId: BatchedCommitDeltaTest's batched() has pod-a/pod-b/pod-c, golden chain-delta-batched-v1.bin has bins/a.seg and bins/b.seg, and BatchingSequencerTest.anExplicitBatchGoesThroughTheWindowRatherThanPastIt submits from("pod0", 0) and from("pod1", 0) -- same flushSeq, and the incarnation would be whatever the one fixture supplies. So an M4.10c author who reads the ADR alone, adds the triple, keeps the fixtures as they stand and asserts the per-segment triple on them, writes a green suite over exactly the hoist the ADR is warning about. A new golden does not save it either: goldens are generated FROM the encoder, so a golden generated from a partial-hoist encoder matches its own bytes; the golden catches later drift, not the shape chosen when it was written.
findings.surviving_mutation: Encode/decode podId per SegmentCommit but incarnationId and flushSeq once per CommitDelta, assigning the single decoded pair to every segment. Under a fixture whose segments differ only in podId this survives (a) CommitDelta round-trip whole-record isEqualTo, (b) an explicit per-segment triple assertion, (c) byte-identity against a golden generated from that same encoder, and (d) BatchingSequencerTest's commitAll assertion. It then drops every pod but one's flushSeq on M5's first forwarded multi-pod batch.
findings.remedy: Say in the ADR what backlog-notes.md:259-265 already says: the fixture must vary incarnationId or flushSeq PER SEGMENT, not merely 'at least one field' -- podId-only variation is what the tree has today and is exactly what the partial hoist survives. Non-blocking because the M4.10c row links those notes and the notes carry the precise form.

findings.claim: The sweep instruction miscounts its own enumeration and the grep it names does not find one of the sites it lists.
findings.failure_scenario: 'AND TEN JAVA SITES ARE THIS ROW'S ... git grep -n 'podId, flushSeq' -- '*.java' finds them' then enumerates ELEVEN: Sequencer.java:35, :46, :88, :51, CommitRequest.java:19, FakeSequencer.java:27, FakeSequencerTest:178, Checkpoint.java:32, IngestCommitPathTest.java:81, CommitProtocolSimulation.java:58, CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest:23. Measured: the grep returns 11 hits over 8 files, and Sequencer.java:51 is NOT among them (its text is 'WITHOUT CHANGING THE RECORD SHAPE', a different phrase), while FakeSequencer.java:29 IS a hit and is not enumerated. An M4.10c session that trusts the count over the enumeration, or trusts the grep to reach every enumerated site, updates the wrong set -- and the falsified javadoc at Sequencer.java:51 is one this row explicitly calls load-bearing, because it is the one promising the record shape does not change.
findings.surviving_mutation: N/A -- this is a false count in a durable prescription, not a weak assertion. The stated harm is the M4.8-named failure the notes themselves cite: fixing one copy of a fact and missing its duplicates.
findings.remedy: Say eleven, or drop the number; and note that Sequencer.java:51 is outside the grep.

round8_items_verified: MAJOR (fixed): fixture-data guidance replaced by an assertion prescription in ADR-0036:119-125 and backlog-notes.md:259-265. The partial hoist IS the surviving one: a podId-only hoist dies on BatchedCommitDeltaTest's whole-record equality (its three segments carry three distinct pods), a full hoist dies on any varying field, and podId-per-segment with the other two hoisted is the maximal survivor over the fixtures as they stand. Confirmed BatchingSequencerTest:261 asserts only .hasSize(2).

MINOR (fixed): ADR-0036:131-135 requires the discriminating golden to be a NEW file beside chain-delta-batched-v1.bin. Consistent with GoldenChainEntryTest, which asserts encode() byte-identity against BOTH existing goldens -- those assertions are what force a version-aware canonical encoding rather than an edited fixture.

MINOR (fixed): ADR-0036:167-171 requires an ENUMERATED {0,1} rather than version <= VERSION, and records that CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest's bytes[7] = 1 stops being an unknown version after the bump. Verified: Checkpoint.java:150-152 reads b.getInt(4) and refuses on `version != VERSION`, and CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest:117 sets bytes[7] = 1 expecting 'unsupported checkpoint version' -- byte 7 is the LSB of that big-endian int, so the test does become vacuous at VERSION = 1.
MINOR (moot): podId is carried on the chain per ADR-0036:98-107, so no pod extractor is needed. Verified SegmentCommit.java:29 checks only isEmpty() and SegmentKey exposes no parser for podShortId.
prescriptions_that_do_kill_their_mutatio: Minting site (ADR-0036:41-47, backlog-notes.md:275-280): 'two DefaultIngest instances sharing a podShortId must record DIFFERENT incarnations, and one instance's two flushes the SAME one'. The second half is the killer -- UUID.randomUUID() beside flushSeq++ inside flushLocked passes the first and fails the second. IngestCommitPathTest already holds a Recording sequencer at the right seam, so this is T0-reachable with no clock, socket or store.

M4.10d anchor (backlog-notes.md, M4.10d): the CheckpointWriterContentTest doesNotContainKey("poda") inversion is stated as an inversion rather than a deletion, and the notes explicitly forbid deleting it as the testing.md rule 5 inversion. Verified the assertion exists at CheckpointWriterContentTest.java:156. The notes also correctly refuse the seed-at-write-time shortcut, which would make containsEntry("poda", 42L) green while the replay still commits twice.
M4.10d discriminator is a POD RESTART, not a takeover -- correct, since a cross-leader fixture has one incarnation and the bare pair passes it.
notes: Tier: every prescribed assertion here is T0 (encode/decode, commitAll against an in-memory store, a recording Sequencer). No clock, socket or object store is pulled in where T0 would do. No design finding.
No test file is staged, so testing.md rule 4-5 (a weakened assertion landing beside a production change) cannot be violated by this commit; check-test-integrity has nothing to judge and neither do I.

SPEC.md acceptance criterion 6 gained the answer-bound clause ('returns the original assignment when the recorded pointer names a delta carrying that triple, refusing otherwise'), and the M4.10d backlog row carries it too. The T0 mutation-table row for it names only 'assigns fresh offsets' and 'keyed on the bare pair' -- not 'answers from the pointed delta unconditionally', which is the silent one (another flush's firstOffset returned). Not raised as a finding because the row states the requirement; worth naming in M4.10d's mutation column when that row is written.
